sovereignty_definition: A StegVerse deployment is sovereign only when every required production process, scheduler, runtime, state store, validation execution boundary, control-plane executor, and continuity dependency is satisfied by the deployment's own sovereign physical host and StegVerse-controlled logical boundaries on that host. No third-party machine or service may be a required production dependency.
allowed_carrier_classes: the deployment's sole StegVerse sovereign physical host
isolated StegVerse logical nodes/processes/state roots created on that same sovereign host
logical_independence_rule: When proof requires independent execution, peer behavior, restart, reconstruction, collision, replay, or isolation, satisfy it with independently identified and isolated logical processes/state roots on the same sovereign physical host whenever technically sufficient; never manufacture a second-machine requirement.
prohibited_required_dependencies: any additional physical machine required solely to prove independence
third_party_optional_input_rule: A user may voluntarily interact with external providers or networks, but loss or unavailability of any such service must not prevent the sovereign StegVerse runtime, governance, proof, replay, reconstruction, continuity, or local control plane from operating within its declared scope.
required_source_enforcement: G18 must not escalate to acquiring or binding another physical machine when same-host logical isolation is technically sufficient
machine_observable_release_condition: The deployment's own sovereign physical host produces activation.latest.json with all required sovereign predicates true. Any independent-peer requirement must be satisfied by isolated same-host StegVerse logical nodes unless a product owner explicitly changes the deployment topology; no third-party machine or hosted platform may satisfy or substitute for that proof.
